module_title: Haloalkanes & Haloarenes: Preparation & Basic Properties (Detailed Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level covers halogen-substituted hydrocarbons. It explores the diverse methods of preparing alkyl and aryl halides, introduces their physical properties, and establishes the groundwork for nucleophilic substitution reactions.

core_concepts.title: Classification and Nomenclature
core_concepts.description:
Haloalkanes (Alkyl Halides, $R-X$) and Haloarenes (Aryl Halides, $Ar-X$). Classified based on the number of halogen atoms (mono, di, polyhalogen) and the hybridization of the carbon atom carrying the halogen:
1. $sp^3$ C-X bond: Alkyl halides ($1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ$), Allylic halides ($C=C-C-X$), Benzylic halides ($Ar-C-X$).
2. $sp^2$ C-X bond: Vinylic halides ($C=C-X$), Aryl halides ($Ar-X$, halogen directly on the benzene ring).

core_concepts.title: Preparation of Haloalkanes
core_concepts.description:
1. From Alcohols: The best method is using Thionyl Chloride ($SOCl_2$). Reaction: $R-OH + SOCl_2 \rightarrow R-Cl + SO_2\uparrow + HCl\uparrow$. This is preferred because both by-products are gases that escape, leaving pure $R-Cl$.
2. From Hydrocarbons: Free radical halogenation of alkanes (gives mixtures). Electrophilic addition of HX to alkenes (follows Markovnikov's rule). Addition of $Br_2/CCl_4$ to alkenes (anti-addition, discharges red-brown color).
3. Halogen Exchange: 
- Finkelstein Reaction: For Alkyl Iodides. $R-Cl/Br + NaI \xrightarrow{\text{dry acetone}} R-I + NaCl/NaBr\downarrow$.
- Swarts Reaction: For Alkyl Fluorides. $R-Cl/Br + AgF/Hg_2F_2 \rightarrow R-F + AgCl/Br\downarrow$.

core_concepts.title: Preparation of Haloarenes
core_concepts.description:
1. Electrophilic Substitution: Direct halogenation of benzene using $Cl_2/Br_2$ in the presence of Lewis acids ($FeCl_3, FeBr_3$) in dark. Iodine requires an oxidizing agent ($HNO_3$) to prevent the reversible reaction.
2. Sandmeyer's Reaction: From primary aromatic amines. Aniline is converted to Diazonium Salt ($Ph-N_2^+Cl^-$) using $NaNO_2 + HCl$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$. The diazonium salt is treated with $Cu_2Cl_2/HCl$ or $Cu_2Br_2/HBr$ to yield Chlorobenzene or Bromobenzene.

core_concepts.title: Physical Properties
core_concepts.description:
1. Boiling Points: For a given alkyl group, BP increases with halogen size: $RI > RBr > RCl > RF$. For isomeric haloalkanes, BP decreases with branching (decreased surface area lowers van der Waals forces). E.g., 1-bromobutane > 2-bromobutane > 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
2. Solubility: Haloalkanes are highly polar but incredibly slightly soluble in water. They cannot form hydrogen bonds with water, nor can they break the strong H-bonds already present between water molecules. They are soluble in organic solvents.

important_entities.name: The Carbon-Halogen Bond Polarity
important_entities.key_fact: Halogens are more electronegative than carbon, making the C-X bond highly polarized ($C^{\delta+}-X^{\delta-}$).
important_entities.significance: This polarity is the driving force for almost all reactions of haloalkanes. The partial positive charge on carbon ($C^{\delta+}$) acts as a magnet for nucleophiles (electron-rich species), initiating Nucleophilic Substitution reactions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive conceptual trap. Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so students assume Methyl Fluoride ($CH_3F$) has the highest dipole moment. WRONG. Dipole moment ($\\mu = q \times d$) depends on both charge and distance. The extremely small size of Fluorine makes the C-F bond length ($d$) very short. Chlorine's larger size creates a longer C-Cl bond, overriding the electronegativity difference. Thus, Dipole Moment order: $CH_3Cl > CH_3F > CH_3Br > CH_3I$.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Finkelstein forms I, Swarts forms F
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Finkelstein is specific for making Iodides (using NaI). Swarts is specific for making Fluorides (using AgF/CoF2). Remember: **F**inkelstein does NOT make **F**luorides.

exam_strategy_tips: In Sandmeyer's reaction, if you want to prepare Iodobenzene, you DO NOT need Cuprous halides ($Cu_2I_2$). Simply warming the diazonium salt with Potassium Iodide (KI) is sufficient to precipitate Iodobenzene.
